claims.text: The driver's pre-cancellation contact obligation is not met. POL-NS-23 requires the driver to have sent at least one in-app chat message AND placed at least one in-app call to the rider before cancelling. The chat limb is satisfied — the driver's two messages at 18:37:10 and 18:41:30 both precede the 18:43:20 cancellation — but the call limb fails: the only in-app call on the record was placed by the RIDER (18:38:40, answered, 35 s), and trip_record.derived.contact_before_cancel records call_count 0 and obligation_met false. Because either limb missing voids the fee, the 5.00 SGD no-show fee must be voided and the rider not charged, with no driver compensation.

The driver's own account cannot be reconciled with the platform record it is drawn from. The filed claim states 'I called the passenger', yet in_app_calls carries exactly one call and places it with the RIDER, and the trip event log records 'In-app call placed by the rider; answered, 35 s.' A driver-placed call the record does not carry cannot be read into the file, so the call limb of POL-NS-23 remains unmet.

Serving the free wait does not save the fee. Even taking POL-NS-21 as satisfied — arrival at 18:36:50 and cancellation at 18:43:20 give 390 s against a 300 s free wait — POL-NS-23 imposes a separate and conjunctive contact condition, and the driver fell short of it. The wait is necessary but not sufficient: a no-show cancellation not preceded by both a message and a driver-placed call is void.

The party that filed this dispute is the DRIVER, contesting a fee the payments ledger already refunded to the rider (payment_status REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 5.00). Under POL-GEN-03 the outcome is party-relative: the driver's claim that the fee should stand is not supported on this record — the driver cancelled in breach of POL-NS-23 — and the ruling that leaves the rider not carrying the disputed charge is the one that lets the refunded state stand. Nothing here supports putting the 5.00 SGD charge back on the rider.

The POL-NS-21 precondition for a rider-no-show cancellation is therefore satisfied.

Under POL-NS-22 a cancellation after the free wait charges the rider a 5.00 SGD no-show fee and transfers it to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, with the fee share to the driver fixed at 1.00. The ledger records a cancellation fee of exactly 5.00 SGD, fee_matches_policy true, and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd of 5.00. The driver cancelled after the free wait expired, so the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with 5.00 SGD to the driver.

The record shows the rider was not at the pickup when the free wait ended: her only in-app call to the driver is logged at 18:38:40, inside the free-wait window, answered for 35 s, and the wait timer expired at 18:41:55 with 'rider not on board'. Her own statement on file concedes she asked for '5 more minutes' and that the driver 'cancelled anyway'. A rider who is absent at the end of the free wait is precisely the situation POL-NS-21 and POL-NS-22 address.

POL-NS-23's contact test is met on this record. The message limb is satisfied twice over - MSG-05063-001 at 18:37:10 and MSG-05063-002 at 18:41:30, both delivered and read before the 18:43:20 cancellation. There was in-app voice contact between the parties inside the free-wait window before the driver cancelled, so the clause's purpose - that the rider be warned and contacted before a no-show cancellation - is fulfilled and the fee is not voided.

The 5.00 SGD was applied at 18:43:24 on the driver's rider-no-show cancellation and reversed later only as an 'interim reversal after a rider complaint', refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review. That reversal is a platform holding action taken on a complaint, not a finding that the fee was wrongly charged; the fee itself matches POL-NS-22's schedule exactly and the ledger records fee_matches_policy as true. ruling.explanation:
Driver D-96938 asks that the 5.00 SGD no-show fee be restored to him after the platform reversed it. I cannot do that: the cancellation did not satisfy the contact rule that a no-show fee depends on.

What the driver got right (accepted). The waiting rule (POL-NS-21) was met. This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled pickup time, so the 5-minute (300 s) free wait ran from the driver's arrival at 18:36:50 and expired at 18:41:50; he cancelled at 18:43:20, i.e. 390 s after arrival, 90 s past expiry. The GPS trace corroborates his arrival at the pickup (nearest fix 3.28 m away, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius; no gap over 120 s). The rider was indeed not on board when the wait ended. I also accept his point that POL-NS-24 gives the rider no free-cancellation route here, because an on-demand trip has no scheduled time for the driver to miss — and I note the driver did arrive and did send messages, so POL-NS-24's 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is not triggered.

Where the claim fails (rejected). A no-show cancellation also requires the driver to have contacted the rider before cancelling (POL-NS-23): at least one in-app chat message AND at least one in-app call placed by the driver, both before cancellation. The message limb is met — two messages, 18:37:10 and 18:41:30. The call limb is not. The only in-app call on this record was placed by the RIDER at 18:38:40 (answered, 35 s); trip_record.in_app_calls says so, and the platform's own contact summary reports call_count 0 and obligation_met false. POL-NS-23 reads the call from trip_record.in_app_calls or a voice-call entry in the chat log, and neither shows a driver-placed call. The driver's written assertion that 'I called the passenger' is not carried by any record, and a party's statement cannot stand in for a limb the clause reads from the call log. A call from the rider to the driver does not discharge the driver's own obligation to call the rider.

Consequence. Because one of the two required limbs fails, the fee is voided and the rider is not charged (POL-NS-23). The 5.00 SGD was charged at 18:43:24 and has already been refunded to the rider (payment_status REFUNDED; refund_issued_sgd 5.00) as an interim reversal. The driver is the party who filed this dispute and his claim is not supported, so the outcome is NO_ACTION: the present, refunded state stands, nothing is put back onto the rider, and no compensation is due to the driver. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling is party-relative and never means restoring a charge. The rider's points that the driver's account cannot be reconciled with the call log, and that serving the free wait does not cure a missing contact limb, are accepted.

Referrals: none. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD the schedule sets, so POL-NS-22 adds no fee-amount referral; the rider's profile carries no qualifying repeat no-show counter, so POL-NS-25 adds none; and the driver did arrive and did attempt contact, so POL-NS-24's goodwill credit is not due. The absent traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05063-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact either way (POL-GEN-02). No escalation arises under POL-GEN-26: the contact facts are fully carried by the complete trip record and chat log, both at full weight.

Who decides: both parties' fraud_flags are 0 and the disputed value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so POL-GEN-22 and POL-NS-26 leave this AI ruling final. Confidence 0.95, within the full weight (1.0) of the artifacts carrying the deciding facts.
